attacksRun.attack: Other prose fields are still stale against the post-D-169 world
attacksRun.evidence: This is the attack my v9 review failed to run, so I ran it exhaustively: a pattern scan for pre-D-169 language over every string field in the artifact. Thirteen hits. Twelve resolve correctly — purpose and leftoverDesignOpenStanding describe the remainder as closed after D-169; the g32NamingV1, g32SpecV1 and g32ThreeLimbV1 roles are historical descriptions of superseded candidates, with the accepted namingV2 and g32ThreeLimbV2 roles carrying the current standing; and two G12/G21 obligation reasons say 'does not record D-167', which remains a true denial. The thirteenth is the predecessorV8 self-version sentence, charged above.

observationsNotFindings: Two role fields describe superseded candidates with conditionals whose condition has since resolved: g32NamingV1 says naming v1 is 'Not recordable until G31 is live' and g32ThreeLimbV1 says the same of the v1 act text. G31 is now live, so read literally those sentences imply both are now recordable, which is false — naming v1 is barred by its own REJECT, and three-limb v2 was the text adopted. I did not charge them. Both are historical entries about artifacts this version does not rest on, the accepted successors are pinned alongside with correct standings, and namingV2's role states plainly that 'Frozen v1 remains REJECT JFXG-V1-B1 and is not recorded'. They are also unchanged from v9, which both reviewers saw. Recorded so the coordinator can decide whether the family wants historical roles frozen at their original tense or refreshed each fold.

The contrast between predecessorV8 and every other predecessor role is the useful lesson here. Five roles use 'Not this artifact's version number', a formulation that cannot go stale no matter how many folds follow. Two use the concrete 'This vN' form, and one of those two is now wrong. The generic form is not merely a style preference; it removes an entire recurring failure mode from the chain, and this corpus has now charged that failure three times.

The fold is otherwise exemplary in scope. The whole obligations array, the whole summary, liveGateOwners, doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone and leftoverDesignOpenStanding are byte-identical to frozen v9, so three corrections to prose and cardinality were made without disturbing a single measurement. That is what made the over-broad-fold attack cheap to refute and what isolates the one remaining defect.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: One SHOULD-FIX, no blockers. All three prior findings are landed and I verified each against frozen v9 and live bytes rather than any reviewer's account: top-level requiredNowUnchanged is now 28 with no bare 26 anywhere; the two D-056 stale sub-claims are rewritten to say JOIN-FX execution is no longer an unnamed remainder and that DR-G32 is live; and the remeasurement clause now names v8, v9, naming v2 and three-limb v2 / D-169 instead of the pre-D-169 set. The fold is tightly scoped — the entire obligations array, the entire summary, liveGateOwners and doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone are byte-identical to v9, so nothing measured moved. What lands is that basedOn.predecessorV8.role still carries 'This v9 remasures after D-169. This v9 does not reuse the v8 version number' into an artifact published as v10, unchanged from v9 where it was correct. This is a regression of the exact defect class the artifact's own predecessorV7.role documents as CLAUDE-DALJ-V7-SF1, and which findingDisposition also carries as CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 — the third time this corpus has met it. Five sibling roles use the immune generic form 'Not this artifact's version number', and the newly added predecessorV9 role gets the concrete form right; predecessorV8 is the only role naming a version and it names the wrong one. I graded it SHOULD-FIX to match the two prior gradings of the same class rather than escalating for the regression. One thing I owe the record: two of the three findings this fold repairs are Codex's, and my v9 verdict missed both. I enumerated d056AuthoringIneligibleReasonStale and moved past it without opening it, and never read v9's remeasurement clause — I let the attack list bound the audit in a version whose whole purpose was remeasurement. This time I scanned every string field for pre-D-169 language, thirteen hits, twelve resolving as historical or denial and one becoming the finding above. 17 attacks run: 15 refuted outright, 1 refuted except as charged, 1 landing.
